title: Natural coefficient map on complexes
statement: Let R,A,B,D be commutative rings, with A and B R-algebras and D an (A tensor_R B)-algebra. Scalar extension and restriction are those of [def-weil-module-base-change], tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and cochain complexes are those of [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. There exists a natural transformation on A-complexes from B tensor_R Res_R(P) to Res_B(D tensor_A P), whose degree-j component sends b tensor p to the image in D of (1 tensor b), tensor p. No flatness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: The two composite ring maps R to D agree by the balancing identity in the tensor algebra. This gives an identity-valued comparison between the corresponding double restrictions.

Transpose the A-to-D scalar-extension unit, after restriction, through the R-to-B scalar-extension adjunction. Adjunction naturality gives a natural transformation on modules. Apply mapHomologicalComplex to get a natural transformation on complexes. The adjunction formula on pure tensors gives exactly the required generator identity.

theorem exists_baseTensorCoefficientNaturalMap :
    ∃ γ : (restrictScalars.{u} (algebraMap R A)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        (extendScalars.{u, u, u} (algebraMap R B)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶
      (extendScalars.{u, u, u} ((algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) D).comp
        (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B)))).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        (restrictScalars.{u} (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) D) ⋙
          restrictScalars.{u} Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℤ),
      ∀ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (j : ℤ) (b : B) (p : P.X j),
        (γ.app P).f j (b ⊗ₜ[R, algebraMap R B] p) =
          (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) D (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight b) ⊗ₜ[A,
            (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) D).comp (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B))] p)
